title: Lesson 39 - Exporting from Salesforce: Data Export, Data Loader export, API, reports
description: Compare and contrast various techniques and considerations for exporting data from Salesforce, including Data Export service, Data Loader export, API-based extraction, and reporting exports, and their suitability for different volumes and purposes.

questions.question: A team needs a recurring nightly feed of changed records to a warehouse. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Bulk API query jobs extracting incrementally by SystemModstamp
questions.explanation: Recurring incremental extraction for a warehouse uses Bulk API/ETL with last-modified filters; Data Export (A) is scheduled backup and reports/list views (C, D) are limited and not for feeds.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Salesforce exports are TRUE?
options: Report exports are limited by row limits and not suited to LDV
Exports include all data regardless of the running user's access
Scheduled Data Export is a coarse backup, not a full point-in-time restore
Exports can be non-selective without performance impact
questions.explanation: Report exports have row limits (A) and Data Export is coarse backup only (C); exports are filtered by the user's access (B false) and LDV exports must be selective (D false).

questions.question: Why must large exports filter on indexed fields?
options: Because non-selective queries time out at LDV, so indexed filters keep extraction performant
questions.explanation: LDV exports must be selective to avoid timeouts; exports do use SOQL (A false) and the other reasons are unrelated.
